slides.title:
Your idea in.
Working software out.
slides.body: I run delivery as a loop — plan, design, build, test, deploy, maintain — with AI agents doing the hands-on work and me above the loop: instigating, directing, governing. Scroll to watch one idea go round.

slides.title: Agents do the hands-on work. I direct it.
slides.body: Your idea becomes a written intent — nothing enters the loop until it’s written down with you. Agents plan it, draft the architecture, build the units in parallel and verify their own work. I make the trade-offs: stack, boundaries, security, cost.

slides.title: Nothing ships without me.
slides.body: The agent that wrote the code can’t approve it. Every change comes back to my desk: I approve, reject or steer — I decide what green means, and quality, security and cost stay my call.

slides.title: Shipped. And kept running.
slides.body: One pipeline ships the product with its documents — this page and my CV included. Then agents watch production and feed what drifts back as new intent; I triage, approve the fix, and the loop turns again.

summary.body: Software architect, seven years in. I’ve designed and shipped business software across shipping and logistics, eKYC, mobile payments and industrial monitoring — mostly on Azure with .NET and NestJS, DDD and microservices — and I bring AI into real products, from architecture to deployment. I run delivery as a loop: AI agents do the hands-on work, my judgement stays above it. Solo, or leading a small team.
